# Jubilees Chapter 28 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 28:3 — "weak eyes" vs. "gentle eyes" (Leah)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Leah's eyes were weak" | Literal: Ge'ez renders Hebrew rakkot — tender/weak |
| LOGOS | "Leah's eyes were weak" | Same; standard scholarly translation |
| PNEUMA | "Leah had gentle eyes" | Gentler interpretation; some scholars read rakkot as "delicate/lovely" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "weak" following EMET/LOGOS. The contrast with Rachel's beauty implies Leah's eyes were a defect, not an asset. "Gentle" softens the narrative tension.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 28:10 — "bridal week" vs. "week of this one"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "complete the week of this one" | Literal Ge'ez phrasing |
| LOGOS | "complete the bridal week for this one" | Adds clarifying context |
| PNEUMA | "finish out this wedding week" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "bridal week" as the clearest rendering. The Ge'ez "week of this one" is a compressed reference to the seven-day wedding celebration; the gloss is warranted.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 28:18 — "bear upon my knees" vs. "give birth on my behalf"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "bear upon my knees" | Literal: the Ge'ez preserves the ancient adoption ritual |
| LOGOS | "give birth on behalf of me" | Functional rendering |
| PNEUMA | "she'll be my surrogate" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "bear upon my knees" with slight smoothing to "give birth on my behalf." The ritual of knees-birth is an ancient adoption gesture (cf. Gen 30:3) that should be retained as it appears in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved as modified EMET.

---

## 28:29 — "God remembered Rachel"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "And God remembered Rachel" | Literal with conjunction |
| LOGOS | "Then God remembered Rachel" | Temporal connector signals the turn |
| PNEUMA | "Then at last God remembered Rachel" | Adds emotional weight |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "Then God remembered Rachel." PNEUMA's "at last" adds editorial emotion not present in the Ge'ez. The "then" is sufficient to signal the narrative turn after the long delay.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
